metadata.title: Code for A Categorical Framework for Khipu Analysis
metadata.description:
Categorical Framework for Khipu Analysis - Code Repository

Description

This repository contains the complete Python implementation of the computational methods described in:

"A Categorical Framework for Khipu Analysis: Computational Methods for Reconstruction and Exploratory Diagnostics"
J. J. Segura, Universidad Andrés Bello (2026)

What This Code Does

This package provides reproducible tools for analyzing khipu (Andean knotted-cord recording devices) using category-theoretic principles. The implementation bridges abstract mathematical frameworks with practical archaeological corpus analysis.

Core Capabilities:

  1. Categorical Signature Extraction: Computes an 8-dimensional structural fingerprint for each khipu based on empirical densities of limit-like and colimit-like patterns (equalizers, pullbacks, products, coproducts, pushouts, terminal objects)

  2. Administrative Backbone Validation: Operationalizes the widespread archaeological hypothesis of summary-detail organization through context-free grammar with numeric side conditions

  3. Exploratory Corpus Diagnostics: Unsupervised clustering, PCA visualization, and weak-label association analysis for identifying structural regimes across large khipu databases

  4. Reconstruction Under Damage: Constraint-propagation algorithms for completing partial khipu descriptions while quantifying uncertainty, motivated by sheaf-theoretic "gluing" principles

  5. Multi-Surrogate Sensitivity Analysis: Evaluates grouping uncertainty by computing signatures under multiple pendant-group surrogates (database clusters, color schemes, spatial contiguity)

Validated on Public Corpora

All methods have been empirically validated on two major public khipu databases:

  • Open Khipu Repository (OKR): 619 khipu, 54,403 cords
  • Harvard Khipu Database (HKDB) export via Khipu Field Guide (v2.1.0): 685 khipu, 62,515 cords

Key Features

  • Reproducible by design: Pinned dependencies, deterministic outputs, complete environment specifications
  • Fast execution: Full corpus analysis (600+ khipu) completes in ~25 seconds
  • Database-agnostic: Works with OKR SQLite format and HKDB KFG exports
  • Extensible: Modular architecture allows custom signature components and constraint families
  • Well-documented: Inline docstrings, example workflows, case studies
  • Archaeological best practices: Respects uncertainty, avoids over-interpretation, provides diagnostic warnings

Installation

Requirements

  • Python 3.11+ (tested on 3.11.2)
  • Core dependencies: numpy, pandas, scipy, scikit-learn, matplotlib, networkx
  • Database support: sqlite3 (built-in)

Quick Start

# Clone repository
git clone [REPOSITORY_URL]
cd khipu-categorical-framework

# Create virtual environment (recommended)
python -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate  # On Windows: venv\Scripts\activate

# Install dependencies
pip install -r requirements.txt
# OR for pinned reproducible environment:
pip install -r requirements_pinned.txt

# Run basic workflow
python examples/basic_workflow.py

Using the Pinned Environment

For exact reproducibility of manuscript results:

# Option 1: pip with pinned requirements
pip install -r requirements_pinned.txt

# Option 2: conda environment (if you use conda)
conda env create -f environment.yml
conda activate khipu-categorical

Usage Examples

Example 1: Compute Signatures for a Single Khipu

from khipu_categorical import KhipuLoader, SignatureExtractor

# Load khipu from OKR database
loader = KhipuLoader("path/to/khipu.db")
khipu = loader.load_khipu(khipu_id="UR004")

# Extract 8-dimensional signature
extractor = SignatureExtractor()
signature = extractor.compute_signature(khipu)

print(f"Equalizer proxy (σ3): {signature['sigma3_equalizer']:.3f}")
print(f"Product proxy (σ2): {signature['sigma2_product']:.3f}")
print(f"Grouping quality (σ9): {signature['sigma9_grouping_quality']:.3f}")

Example 2: Run Full Corpus Analysis

from khipu_categorical import CorpusAnalyzer

# Analyze entire OKR corpus
analyzer = CorpusAnalyzer("path/to/khipu.db")
results = analyzer.run_full_analysis(
    grouping_surrogates=["cluster", "color", "contiguity"],
    output_dir="results/"
)

# Results include:
# - Signature statistics with bootstrap 95% CIs
# - PCA visualizations
# - Cross-surrogate correlation tables
# - Case study reports

Example 3: Reconstruct Damaged Khipu

from khipu_categorical import ReconstructionEngine

# Load partial khipu with missing values
partial_khipu = loader.load_khipu("UR123", allow_missing=True)

# Attempt reconstruction
engine = ReconstructionEngine(tolerance=0.05)
completions = engine.reconstruct(
    partial_khipu,
    max_solutions=10,
    constraint_types=["summation", "hierarchy", "scheme_repetition"]
)

# Examine uncertainty
print(f"Found {len(completions)} consistent completions")
print(f"Variable uncertainty ranges: {engine.get_uncertainty_summary()}")

Reproducing Manuscript Results

All tables and figures in the manuscript can be reproduced exactly:

# Generate all OKR results (Tables 4-6, Figures 5-6, 11-12)
python manuscript_reproduction/run_okr_analysis.py

# Generate all HKDB results (Tables 7-9, Figures 7-8)
python manuscript_reproduction/run_hkdb_analysis.py

# Generate all figures
python manuscript_reproduction/generate_all_figures.py

# Generate all tables (LaTeX format)
python manuscript_reproduction/generate_all_tables.py

Expected runtime: ~25 seconds per corpus on modern hardware (tested on [specify your system]).

Data Sources

This code works with two public khipu databases:

Open Khipu Repository (OKR)

  • Format: SQLite database (khipu.db)
  • Citation: OKR Team (2025). The Open Khipu Repository, v2.1.0. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18025748
  • Download: https://zenodo.org/records/18025748

Harvard Khipu Database (HKDB) Export

  • Format: Processed via Khipu Field Guide tooling
  • Citation: Medrano & Khosla (2024). How Can Data Science Contribute to Understanding the Khipu Code? (Companion Data), v2.1.0. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.10472429
  • Download: https://zenodo.org/records/10472429
  • Processing: See Khipu Field Guide documentation at khipufieldguide.com

Note: Khipu are cultural heritage objects. Users should interpret analyses in collaboration with source communities and domain experts.

Validation and Testing

The package includes comprehensive tests:

# Run all tests

# Run with coverage report
pytest --cov=khipu_categorical tests/

# Run specific test suite

All tests pass on the reference environment (Python 3.11.2, see requirements_pinned.txt).

  • Full HKDB corpus analysis (685 khipu): ~24 seconds
  • Reconstruction (10 missing values, 5 iterations): ~0.5 seconds

Known Issues and Limitations

  1. Grouping detection: Pendant-group surrogates are heuristic. Signature stability (σ9) should be checked before interpreting equalizer proxies.

  2. Decoding ambiguity: The value functor V is partial. Khipu with ambiguous knot sequences may have unstable signatures.

  3. Reconstruction scope: Current constraint families focus on additive relations and scheme repetition. Richer constraint types are planned for future versions.

  4. Database formats: Currently supports OKR SQLite and HKDB KFG exports. Other formats require conversion.

  5. Computational limits: Reconstruction with >50 missing values and >100 constraints may be slow without optimization.

See manuscript Section 10.2 for detailed discussion of interpretive limitations.

metadata.title: Inca Quipu: Pre-Columbian Algorithmic Data Structures
metadata.description: The Inca Empire, a monumental civilization flourishing in pre-Columbian South America, is renowned for its sophisticated societal organization and administrative prowess, achieved notably without a conventional alphabetic writing system. Instead, the Incas developed and extensively utilized the quipu (also spelled khipu), an intricate system of knotted cords, for recording and transmitting information. While traditionally viewed primarily as a numerical accounting tool, contemporary research suggests that quipu represented a far more complex information encoding system, bearing striking resemblances to modern algorithmic data structures. This paper posits that quipu functioned not merely as static repositories of data but as dynamic, three-dimensional systems capable of hierarchical organization, relational encoding, and potentially narrative expression, reflecting algorithmic principles. By analyzing the structural components of quipu—main cords, pendant cords, subsidiary cords, knot types, positions, colors, and ply directions—through the lens of computer science, we explore how these elements facilitated complex data storage, retrieval, and manipulation. This interdisciplinary approach aims to illuminate the intellectual sophistication of Inca information management, re-evaluating quipu as advanced pre-Columbian algorithmic data structures that underpinned the administrative, economic, and potentially historical fabric of one of the largest empires of the ancient world.

title: Inca Quipu: Pre-Columbian Algorithmic Data Structures

metadata.title: Knot Theory and the Information Capacity of Inca Quipu
metadata.description: The Inca Quipu, an ancient Andean knot-based recording device, represents one of history's most sophisticated non-alphabetic information systems. Despite extensive research, its full information capacity and the extent of its communicative potential remain largely undeciphered, particularly beyond its well-established use in numerical accounting. This paper explores the application of knot theory as a novel mathematical framework to analyze the structural complexity and inherent information encoding capabilities of quipu. We propose that the diverse forms, configurations, and arrangements of knots, cords, and their interconnections, beyond mere numerical values, might encapsulate a rich, topologically defined information layer. By conceptualizing quipu elements as knot-theoretic objects, we aim to quantify potential information states, offering new insights into how intricate topological properties could have been utilized for advanced data storage or even narrative representation. Our methodology outlines how knot invariants and topological classifications can reveal hidden patterns and structural grammar within quipu constructions, thereby contributing to a deeper understanding of this remarkable pre-Columbian communication technology and suggesting avenues for a more comprehensive decipherment.

title: Knot Theory and the Information Capacity of Inca Quipu

metadata.title: Formal Systems and Data Structures in Andean Khipu
metadata.description: The Andean khipu, an enigmatic system of knotted cords used by the Inca Empire and earlier Andean civilizations, represents a profound challenge to conventional understandings of information storage and communication. This paper explores khipu from the integrated perspective of formal systems and data structures, analyzing their physical attributes as components of a structured language for encoding and retrieving information. By examining knot types, cord colors, ply directions, and hierarchical arrangements, we propose that khipu functioned as sophisticated, three-dimensional data structures capable of representing both numerical and, potentially, narrative data. We review historical interpretations and contemporary research efforts, including computational approaches, that aim to unlock the full expressive power of khipu. The methodology involves a theoretical framework that maps khipu elements to formal system primitives, highlighting analogies with modern computational concepts such as linked lists and hierarchical databases. Our results suggest that the inherent modularity and rule-based construction of khipu allowed for complex information management, crucial for the administration of the vast Inca Empire. The discussion emphasizes the implications of this perspective for understanding pre-Columbian intellectual achievements and offers avenues for future interdisciplinary research into these unique artifacts, while also considering the ethical dimensions of such studies.

title: Formal Systems and Data Structures in Andean Khipu

metadata.title: Andean Information Systems: Quipu, Metrology, and the Engineering of Empire
metadata.description: The Inca Empire, or Tawantinsuyu, stands as a remarkable testament to sophisticated statecraft in the absence of a traditional alphabetic writing system. Its administrative prowess, managing a vast and diverse territory encompassing millions of people, relied critically on an intricate network of information systems. This paper delves into the symbiotic relationship between the quipu, a complex system of knotted cords used for data storage and communication, and the underlying principles of Andean metrology. We argue that these two elements, far from being isolated cultural artifacts, constituted a cohesive and deliberately engineered information infrastructure that enabled the Inca state to effectively govern, mobilize resources, manage populations, and construct its formidable imperial apparatus. By analyzing historical accounts, archaeological findings, and the mathematical properties of quipu and Inca measurement units, this study illuminates how the precise collection, standardized measurement, and efficient transmission of data through these systems were fundamental to the engineering, maintenance, and expansion of the pre-Columbian Andean empire. The paper contributes to understanding non-alphabetic information technologies and the ingenuity of indigenous administrative solutions in complex societies.

title: Andean Information Systems: Quipu, Metrology, and the Engineering of Empire

metadata.title: Quipu and the Hubble Tension: Cosmic Superstructures as Settling Field Signatures
metadata.description:
The Settling Field framework predicts that H₀ measurements are path-dependent — photons traveling through dense cosmic structures accumulate a larger metric correction than photons traveling through voids, producing a systematic direction-dependence in the measured Hubble constant. The recent discovery of Quipu (Böhringer et al. 2025), the largest known structure in the Universe at 400 Mpc length and 2×10¹⁷ M☉, provides a direct observational test of this prediction.
The Böhringer et al. discovery paper independently identifies that Quipu affects H₀ measurements through streaming motions and the integrated Sachs-Wolfe effect. This paper provides the specific physical mechanism — the path-dependent vacuum field correction — and derives three testable predictions using existing SDSS, DESI, and CMB data: a measurable H₀ anisotropy in Quipu’s sky footprint, a redshift excess in background objects behind Quipu, and a CMB cold region coincident with Quipu’s cluster catalog.
The H₀ gradient with path length is already present in published measurements, decreasing monotonically from ~73.7 km/s/Mpc at 150 Mpc to 67.4 km/s/Mpc at 13,800 Mpc — consistent with the settling field prediction. Independent confirmation of the 8.31% denaturation fraction comes from Abdel-Sattar’s Causal Field Theory (Al-Azhar University, 2025-2026), which derives 8.29% from a completely different first principle.
All three predictions are testable with existing data. No new observations are required.

title: Quipu and the Hubble Tension: Cosmic Superstructures as Settling Field Signatures

metadata.title: Quipu and the Resolution Hypothesis: Five Observational Predictions for a Primordial Filament
metadata.description:
The recent discovery of the Quipu superstructure—a continuous filamentary network spanning over 400 Mpc—presents a significant stress test for the standard ΛCDM cosmological model. While hierarchical assembly permits large structures, the probability of forming a coherent system of this magnitude from Gaussian initial conditions is statistically low.

This paper applies the Resolution Cosmology framework (v5.2/v1.1) to interpret Quipu not as a transient gravitational overdensity, but as a "primordial resolution stroke"—a fossilized feature of the "Deep Strata" established at the Planck epoch. We outline five falsifiable predictions distinguishing this hypothesis from standard gravitational instability, including:

  1. CMB Alignment: A predicted correlation between the Quipu major axis and the CMB "Axis of Evil" (low-ℓ CMB multipoles (l=2 quadrupole and l=3 octopole)).

  2. Velocity Coherence: Bulk flows persisting beyond the standard 150 Mpc decorrelation limit.

  3. Angular Momentum Memory: Galaxy spin alignment scaling with the filament, a prediction recently validated at the 15 Mpc scale by Tudorache et al. (2025).

metadata.title: The Analog Computer State: Quipu, Yupana and the Origins of Computational Sovereignty
metadata.description: This article develops a theoretical interpretation of the Inca administrative system as an early form of computational governance grounded in non-textual registration regimes. Drawing on Registration Regime Theory (RRT), the study argues that the Inca state did not rely on writing but on a programmable infrastructure combining quipu as a hierarchical and semantically encoded memory system and yupana as a computational device. Together, these formed an analog architecture capable of data storage, relational modeling, aggregation, and decision-making. This challenges writing-centered narratives of state formation and proposes a deeper historical ontology of sovereignty based on the capacity to register, compute, and stabilize social reality. The article situates quipu within a long trajectory from ritual memory to algorithmic governance and demonstrates structural continuities between Inca administration and contemporary digital infrastructures such as databases, artificial intelligence, and blockchain systems. The study concludes that sovereignty historically emerges not only from coercion or ideology but from the ability to construct computable reality.

title: The Analog Computer State: Quipu, Yupana and the Origins of Computational Sovereignty

metadata.title: The Algorithmic Andes: Quipu, Roads, and the Logic of Inca Imperial Control
metadata.description: The Inca Empire, Tawantinsuyu, remains one of history's most compelling examples of sophisticated statecraft achieved without a phonetic writing system. This paper argues that the Inca's extraordinary capacity for imperial control rested on an "algorithmic logic" embodied in two interconnected administrative pillars: the quipu (khipu) knot-record system and the vast Qhapaq Ñan road network. The quipu functioned as a non-textual data processing and storage system, enabling precise census counts, tribute accounting, and resource management through standardized, rule-based knot configurations. Simultaneously, the Qhapaq Ñan provided the physical infrastructure for rapid communication, logistical support, and the efficient dissemination and collection of quipu-encoded information across diverse Andean landscapes. By examining how these two systems operated in conjunction, this research reveals a highly systematic, procedural approach to governance, akin to an "algorithm" in its structured inputs, processes, and outputs. This perspective offers a novel framework for understanding the Inca's administrative genius, demonstrating how a pre-modern state effectively managed a vast multi-ethnic empire through sophisticated non-literate information technology and logistical networks, providing a deeper insight into the complexities of ancient imperial control beyond the traditional emphasis on military power and monumental architecture.

title: The Algorithmic Andes: Quipu, Roads, and the Logic of Inca Imperial Control

metadata.title: Inca Imperial Algorithms: Quipu, Qhapaq Ñan, and the Calculi of Spatial Control
metadata.description: The Inca Empire, a vast and complex civilization in pre-Columbian South America, managed its expansive territory and diverse populations through sophisticated administrative and logistical systems, despite lacking an alphabetic writing system. This paper explores two fundamental "imperial algorithms": the quipu and the Qhapaq Ñan. The quipu, a system of knotted cords, served as a primary data storage and communication device, enabling the meticulous recording of census data, tribute obligations, and historical narratives in a decimal positional system. Concurrently, the Qhapaq Ñan, an extensive road network spanning approximately 40,000 kilometers, acted as the physical backbone of the empire, facilitating rapid communication via chasquis (runners), efficient movement of goods and military forces, and the physical imposition of state control across challenging Andean terrains. By analyzing these two intertwined systems, this study argues that the Incas developed highly effective, non-literate calculi for spatial control, information management, and resource allocation. This research employs an interdisciplinary approach, drawing from archaeology, ethnohistory, and systems theory, to elucidate how these "algorithms" were designed, implemented, and maintained to sustain imperial cohesion and project power across an extraordinary geographical range. The paper concludes that the Inca's innovative solutions represent a unique and powerful model of governance and logistical prowess in the ancient world, offering valuable insights into the diversity of complex administrative systems.

title: Inca Imperial Algorithms: Quipu, Qhapaq Ñan, and the Calculi of Spatial Control

metadata.title: The Knots That Sing: An Acoustic Decipherment of the Inca Khipu
metadata.description: This paper proposes that a significant class of Khipu — the knotted cord system of the Inca Empire (c. 1400-1533 CE) — encodes not administrative data but acoustic performance notation: a complete musical score system for Andean chanting and instrumental performance. Three convergent pillars of evidence are presented: (1) structural analysis demonstrating that Khipu physical architecture maps precisely onto musical score logic across eight dimensions — main cord as timeline, pendant cord length as phrase duration, knot vertical position as pitch level, knot type as note quality, cord color as voice/instrument category, and subsidiary cords as harmonic ornaments; (2) physical acoustic validation showing that the average primary cord length of 61 cm calculates to D4 (~95.7% accuracy), a primary Andean chanting pitch, with pendant cord lengths spanning exactly two octaves of the Inca pentatonic scale; and (3) cross-civilizational corroboration with the Andean Siku panpipe, which uses identical length-equals-pitch encoding logic, and whose two-voice ira/arka structure directly mirrors the Khipu pendant/subsidiary cord duality. Published researcher Sabine Hyland has independently identified a phonetic/sound connection in cord colors, consistent with the acoustic framework. This paper integrates with the resonance notation hypothesis established for the Indus Valley Script (Rios, 2026a; DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.19106373), Vinca Script (Rios, 2026b; DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.19139793), and Rongorongo (Rios, 2026c; DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.19140710), forming a unified four-civilization acoustic knowledge framework. Five falsifiable predictions are provided. Copyright © 2026 Abelardo Rios Jr.

title: The Knots That Sing: An Acoustic Decipherment of the Inca Khipu

metadata.title: Khipu and Qhapaq Ñan: The Algorithmic Infrastructure of the Inca Empire
metadata.description: The Inca Empire, Tawantinsuyu, represents a pinnacle of pre-Columbian organizational complexity, uniquely distinguished by its lack of an alphabetic writing system. Despite this, the empire managed to govern an expansive and diverse territory through highly sophisticated administrative and logistical means. This paper posits that the khipu, a system of knotted cords used for record-keeping, and the Qhapaq Ñan, an extensive road network, constituted an integrated "algorithmic infrastructure" crucial for the empire's operation. We argue that these two elements functioned synergistically: khipu encoded vast amounts of quantitative and potentially narrative data, while the Qhapaq Ñan served as the physical conduit for the rapid transmission of these records and the efficient movement of resources, labor, and military personnel based on the information contained within them. By conceptualizing the khipu and Qhapaq Ñan as an interconnected system for data processing, command execution, and feedback, this study sheds new light on the Inca's ingenious approach to information management and imperial control. This perspective moves beyond viewing these components in isolation, instead highlighting their dynamic interrelationship as a foundational element of Inca statecraft and governance.

title: Khipu and Qhapaq Ñan: The Algorithmic Infrastructure of the Inca Empire

metadata.title: Reading the Inca Spreadsheet: How Khipu Knots Encode a Syllabic Data Language
metadata.description:
We propose that the Andean khipu is a structured data archive carrying numbers and text simultaneously on the same physical medium. Computational analysis of the Open Khipu Repository (619 khipus, 54,403 cords, 110,677 knots) identifies a syllabic content channel encoded in long-knot turn counts, complementing the established decimal number system (Locke 1923).

A 13-symbol syllabary with 3 position-dependent alternations (16 effective symbols), derived by brute-force optimization and independently replicated (p = 0.004), achieves approximately 97% lexical coverage on testable text-bearing cords. The syllabary produces archaeologically grounded results:

  • A toponymic system confirmed by colonial-era Andean place names
  • Personal names and kinship terms consistent with documented Andean social structure
  • At least eight distinct document types: tribute registers, cadastral surveys, censuses, judicial dossiers, oracle records, identity registers, administrative texts, and an astronomical catalog — all structured forms, none prose

Three structural discoveries further support the framework: empty cords function as section separators, subsidiary cord color encodes thematic chronology (37% of corpus, 7× chance expectation), and in-situ Quechua-Aymara bilingualism is confirmed.

The khipu is neither a counting device nor a writing system in the literary sense. It is the Inca equivalent of a spreadsheet, and we can now read it as one.

All data, code, and translations are publicly available. We invite replication, critique, and collaboration from Andean specialists.

metadata.title: LA HISTORIA SIN ESCRITURA: EL ENIGMA DEL QUIPU "ROSETTA" Y LAS PANACAS INKAS.
metadata.description:
La cultura inka, notable por su gran desarrollo sin escritura gráfica, utilizó el quipu (sistema de nudos y cuerdas) como principal método de comunicación. La naturaleza del quipu es debatida: Gary Urton postula una función narrativa, Frank Solomon lo limita a lo matemático, mientras Manuel Medrano sugiere una función mnemotécnica, perspectiva que guía esta investigación.

Objetivos e Hipótesis

Objetivo Primario es demostrar la dialéctica operativa de las panacas como depósitos históricos.

 Objetivo Secundario es evaluar las tesis del "quipu Rosetta".

La tesis central es que los Inkas carecieron de un sistema de escritura formal porque las Panacas conservaron eficazmente la historia y el saber mediante métodos orales mnemotécnicos durante siglos, lo cual hace extremadamente compleja la búsqueda de un equivalente al quipu Rosetta.

Conclusiones Finales:

El Imperio Inkaico no desarrolló escritura gráfica por la falta de una necesidad funcional imperante. En su lugar, el Estado se apoyó en un eficaz sistema mnemotécnico-oral centrado en las panacas reales. Este se articuló mediante la interdependencia entre los quipus, los especialistas quipucamayocs y el particular mecanismo de sucesión dinástica.

La probabilidad de hallar un "Quipu Rosetta" es muy baja. Esto se debe a la ausencia de un scriptorium incaico con correspondencia alfabética. El quipu fue un código altamente especializado y de origen autónomo en los Andes, contrastando con las escrituras del Viejo Mundo desarrolladas por un intenso intercambio cultural.

metadata.title: Quipu, Codex, and Cosmos: Epistemic Landscapes of Power in Pre-Columbian Mesoamerica and the Andes
metadata.description: This paper explores the intricate relationship between knowledge systems, cosmological understandings, and the exercise of power in pre-Columbian Mesoamerica and the Andes, focusing on the material forms of quipu and codices. These complex artifacts were not merely repositories of information but served as dynamic epistemic landscapes, structuring perception, reinforcing social hierarchies, and mediating human interactions with the sacred cosmos. By undertaking a comparative analysis, we illuminate how distinct materialities and semiotic approaches (the knotted cords of the Andes versus the pictorial and hieroglyphic manuscripts of Mesoamerica) facilitated similar fundamental functions: record-keeping, historical legitimation, ritual guidance, and the maintenance of political and religious authority. We argue that understanding these instruments requires an interdisciplinary perspective that integrates archaeological, anthropological, and art historical insights to appreciate their sophisticated roles in shaping the power dynamics and worldviews of ancient American civilizations. The study reveals how access to, and interpretation of, these knowledge systems were intrinsically linked to the consolidation and reproduction of elite power, casting the quipu and codex as central to the epistemic ordering of pre-colonial societies.

title: Quipu, Codex, and Cosmos: Epistemic Landscapes of Power in Pre-Columbian Mesoamerica and the Andes

metadata.title: PKS v1.1 — Protocolo Khipu Soberano: Integridad Decisional en la Era de la Abundancia Sintética
metadata.description:
Especificación técnica normativa del Protocolo Khipu Soberano (PKS) v1.1: protocolo offline-first y estándar de evidencia para operar nodos de decisión soberanos bajo condiciones hostiles reales — apagones, aislamiento, conectividad intermitente, y abundancia sintética (el régimen donde imágenes, documentos y órdenes pueden fabricarse a costo marginal cero mediante IA generativa). Implementa los requisitos de IR-STD-v1.0 mediante un régimen de verificación donde cada reclamo crítico mapea a un ID de Protocolo (SKP-PROT-*), cada protocolo produce un Evidence Pack (.irpack) verificable offline, y la ausencia de cualquier artefacto requerido produce el estatus "Not Proven" (comportamiento fail-closed).

Componentes normativos: (1) Khipu Digital — registro de eventos append-only enlazado por hash que constituye el almacén autoritativo (alineado con arquitecturas de procedencia genómica verificadas); (2) Evidence Packs — testigos digitales portátiles capaces de atestiguar en procedimientos años después de su creación; (3) Segmentación IRM Digital mediante ORFC (Oriented Relative Fuzzy Connectedness) — conectividad orientada bajo incertidumbre anclada a Nodos Semilla constitucionales que distingue evidencia admisible de ruido inyectado sin conectividad central; (4) Kill Switch físico dual-control a nivel circuito con prueba negativa obligatoria de imposibilidad de activación remota; (5) QR Bridge con pruebas de liveness resistentes a replay mediante tokens HMAC (HMAC(secret, run_id || step_id || timestamp)) para anclaje criptográfico de procedencia.

Estado de Validación (TRL 4→6): Esta edición documenta la fase de validación científica y algorítmica (Technology Readiness Level 4 a 6), enfocada en verificación de propiedades de integridad, análisis de rendimiento bajo restricciones de recursos, y pruebas controladas en laboratorio. El Apéndice Y documenta la matriz de brechas de implementación con honestidad de TRL: 1 protocolo implementado, 2 parciales, 7 pendientes de validación experimental, y 2 de especificación-solo para fase posterior (requieren hardware GPIO). La Fase 1 ("Tambo Digital") se limita exclusivamente a datos sintéticos clasificados NSD-0 (sin datos sensibles, sin identificadores personales), con operación en hardware commodity de laboratorio (Raspberry Pi 4 equivalente).

Audiencia: Directores de gestión de emergencias, operadores de infraestructura crítica, ingenieros de sistemas distribuidos, custodios institucionales, verificadores independientes, y revisores científicos de arquitecturas de integridad decisional.

metadata.title: Codifying a Cosmos: The Integrated Information System of Quipu, Chasqui Messengers, and the Qhapaq Ñan in Inca Imperial Governance
metadata.description: The Inca Empire, or Tawantinsuyu, stands as a remarkable example of a complex state society that achieved vast territorial control and sophisticated administrative capacity without a system of graphic writing. This paper investigates the integrated information system that underpinned Inca imperial governance, a tripartite structure composed of the quipu (knotted-cord records), the chasqui messenger relay system, and the Qhapaq Ñan (the Great Inca Road). We argue that these three components were not independent elements but formed a cohesive, synergistic network for data collection, storage, transmission, and processing that was fundamental to the empire's political, economic, and military operations. The quipu served as a high-density, portable data storage device, encoding complex numerical and categorical information. The Qhapaq Ñan functioned as the physical network backbone, an engineering marvel that facilitated high-speed, reliable transport across some of the world's most challenging terrain. The chasquis acted as the living data packets, ensuring the rapid and secure transmission of information along this network. By analyzing these elements as an integrated system, this study moves beyond viewing them as isolated curiosities and instead positions them as a sophisticated solution to the universal challenges of imperial administration. Through a synthesis of archaeological evidence, colonial-era chronicles, and modern information theory, this paper demonstrates how the codification of the Andean cosmos through this system enabled the Inca state to manage tribute, mobilize armies, conduct censuses, and maintain social control over millions of subjects across a territory spanning from modern-day Colombia to Chile. The system's elegance, efficiency, and reliance on non-literate forms of data management offer critical insights into the diverse strategies of human statecraft and the material basis of power in pre-Columbian America.

title: Codifying a Cosmos: The Integrated Information System of Quipu, Chasqui Messengers, and the Qhapaq Ñan in Inca Imperial Governance

metadata.title: Production and Laser Dye Printing Method of Textile Patterns Based on Inca Dark Constellation Data.
metadata.description: This art piece is a commissioned work under the I_C project and a collaboration between textile arts and astronomical institutions. The I_C project was initiated by Maria Jose Ríos and sponsored by the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA), located in the Andes Mountains, involving multiple artists in a cross-national cooperation. The project aims to view contemporary and traditional skies from a perspective that combines modern astronomical technology and cultural astronomy. It visualizes modern astronomical data in textile designs to recreate the dark constellation culture in Inca culture. The main objectives of this experiment are twofold: firstly, to establish the range and coordinates of the fictional ancient Inca dark constellations in contemporary astronomical databases, creating a clear contemporary astronomical definition for ancient astronomical cultures that lack specific definitions. Secondly, to design a data visualization method for the dark constellation data, transforming the data into artistic images and using a DIY laser machine and cyanotype printing to print the results of the astronomical data visualization onto natural fibers through optical exposure.

metadata.title: Tawa Pukllay Proof: New Method for Solving Arithmetic Operations with The Inca Yupana Using Pattern Recognition and Parallelism
metadata.description:
Yupana is an Inca device used for arithmetic operations. This article describes a new arithmetical system: Tawa Pukllay (TP), where arithmetic operations do not require mental calculations: no carries, no borrows, no memorization of multiplication tables, nor trial and error procedures for divisions. Instead, user recognizes patterns and makes predefined movements to perform the four basic arithmetic operations very quickly; moreover, the result of the operation can be reached by multiple paths and in parallel, allowing each user to create his own strategies. This paper proves with mathematical rigor that TP produces correct numerical results. 

Special note:
This article constitutes the foundation of a new arithmetic paradigm distinct from the Indo-Arabic system popularized by Brahmagupta: YITP is the Pattern Arithmetic Paradigm. This approach redefines arithmetic as a process of pattern recognition and structured movement rather than symbolic calculation, as developed in the Yupana Inka Tawa Pukllay (YITP) method. Furthermore, this method reclaims the Yupana not merely as an abacus, but as an authentic computing device — the oldest known arithmetic computer in the world — since it requires no mental calculations whatsoever, operating entirely through predefined mechanical movements.
keywords: inca mathematics; tawa pukllay; yupana; pattern recognition; parallel computation; decoding algorithm
